- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.67), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for negative sentiment.
- After a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >5% above recent mean), model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak or adjust downward by 20–30%.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply mean reversion by subtracting 0.1–0.2 from forecast if sentiment is neutral.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term mean reversion; if 10+ days of sentiment >0.67, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overestimation.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, -0.67, 0.67), model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 10–15% for such oscillating sentiment patterns.
